tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Get the Help Scout user the credential belongs to (name, email, role, timezone)

tools.name: list_mailboxes
tools.description: List the Help Scout inboxes (mailboxes) the credential can see

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List Help Scout conversations, optionally filtered by status, inbox or search query

status.description: Conversation status filter (Help Scout defaults to active)

mailbox.description: Optional inbox id to filter by, or comma-separated ids (e.g. 123,567)

query.description: Optional advanced search query, e.g. (subject:"rainbow") or (tag:"vip")

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: Get one Help Scout conversation by ID (subject, status, assignee, primary customer)

needs_review: NO LONGER BLOCKED on auth, and the swap is applied. Help Scout's Inbox (Mailbox) API v2 has NO static API key. https://developer.helpscout.com/mailbox-api/overview/authentication/ documents OAuth2 only, in two flows: authorization_code (issues access_token + refresh_token) and client_credentials (application id + secret, issues an access token and NO refresh token). Both of the two changes this draft said it needed have now landed, so auth.type is 'oauth2_client_credentials' against token_url https://api.helpscout.net/v2/oauth2/token, clientIdField client_id, clientSecretField client_secret, client_auth 'form' (Help Scout's docs put both in the POST body, not in a Basic header). This closes the LIFECYCLE gap that was the real defect: the connector now mints and re-mints its own token rather than depending on an access token pasted into api_key that expires after 172800 seconds with no renewal path.

UNBLOCKED since this draft was written: Connector Spec v1 now HAS the grant. auth.type 'oauth2_client_credentials' is in specSchema.js AUTH_TYPES, validated with token_url + clientIdField + clientSecretField + optional scope/grant_type/client_auth/extra_form; declarativeRuntime.js getClientCredentialsToken mints the token with grant_type=client_credentials, caches it for expires_in minus a buffer, single-flights concurrent calls and keys the cache per pooled instance so a token never crosses tenants; and the shape-proof harness lists the type in TOKEN_FLOW_AUTH_TYPES, probing the API surface with a dummy bearer. The earlier finding that spec v1 could not express this is now STALE.

VAULT-SIDE BLOCKER LIFTED by an ADDITIVE change: services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js 'helpscout' now carries client_id and client_secret alongside api_key, and the generated copies (src/config/integrationTypes.js, services/auth/config/integration-types.export.json) were regenerated by scripts/sync-integration-types.mjs, which a drift test enforces. requiredFields here is now client_id + client_secret, mirroring the vault field keys as the docker_hub draft requires.

the new client_id and client_secret vault fields are required:false ON PURPOSE, so the addition could not invalidate credentials already stored against this type. The consequence is honest and worth stating: a helpscout credential saved before this change holds only api_key, so this CONNECTOR will throw 'missing credential field client_id' on its first call until the user edits the vault entry. The vault UI will not warn them, because the fields are optional there. Nothing regresses today because this is a draft, but promotion needs that migration story decided.

the vault TEST path still exercises the LEGACY token field, and deliberately so: testEndpoint/testMethod/testHeaders for this type were left untouched, so the vault's live test still sends 'Authorization: Bearer <api_key>' against /v2/users/me and proves only that a pasted token works. It does NOT exercise the client-credentials exchange this connector now uses, so a green vault test is not evidence this connector can authenticate. api_key therefore stays in the registry (existing stored credentials keep testing green) while it is NO LONGER in this spec's requiredFields. Modernising testHeaders to mint a token the way the connector does is a separate AUTH-SIDE decision, out of scope for this file.

the wire format of an authenticated call did NOT change in the swap, which is why nothing else in this file moved: Help Scout expects 'Authorization: Bearer <access token>' on every v2 call either way. What changed is WHERE the token comes from (a minted, renewable one rather than a pasted api_key that expires after 172800 seconds, 2 days, documented). base_url, every path, every pick, the clamps and the rateLimit are untouched by the auth change.
READ-ONLY by design: no tool is marked write:true. The v2 API has create/update/delete endpoints for conversations, threads, customers and tags; none is modelled.

paths and every picked field name are taken verbatim from the official endpoint pages (users/me, mailboxes/list, conversations/list, conversations/get), NOT from a live 2xx: the shape-proof stops at 401, so no body was ever data. A wrong pick source yields empty output silently, so the first run with a real token must confirm them.

the API answers application/hal+json, so lists arrive as {_embedded: {mailboxes|conversations: [...]}, page: {...}}. applyPick names an array output from its KEY, so the output keys read '_embedded.mailboxes' and '_embedded.conversations' rather than 'mailboxes' / 'conversations'. Functional but ugly (same handling as the monday precedent).

GET /v2/conversations has no result-size parameter: pagination is page-only with a server-chosen page size, so page is clamped 1/100 and no limit clamp exists to apply. embed=threads is deliberately not exposed (it returns truncated chat threads by design and inflates the payload).
GET /v2/conversations/{id} answers 301 Moved Permanently for a merged conversation, with the new URI in the Location header for 60 days and a 404 after that. The runtime does not follow the redirect.
rateLimit 30/min is a local courtesy and spend guard chosen here; it is not Help Scout's documented ceiling (their rate-limiting page publishes per-plan limits rather than one number).

shape-proof re-run 2026-09-12 AFTER the auth swap, unchanged from 2026-09-11 and still overall SHAPE_PROVEN, runner line verbatim: 'helpscout  SHAPE_PROVEN  proven=5 authwall=0 ambiguous=0 failed=0 inconclusive=0 skipped=0'. The proof artifact now also carries the harness note 'oauth2_client_credentials auth: probed with a dummy bearer token; the token-acquisition flow is NOT proven by this run.', which is the honest limit of this evidence: the API surface is proven, the token exchange is not, and cannot be blind. All five real paths answer 401 with {"error_description":"The access token is invalid or has expired","error":"invalid_token"} (that key order is what the wire returns), while the bogus control path answers a different 404 {"message":"no route and no API found with those values"}, so host, TLS, base_url, the bearer header and every route are proven distinct from the control. What the proof does NOT cover: the OAuth2 token acquisition above, which no blind run can exercise, and no response body was ever data.
